title: 23 Things They Don’t Tell You About Capitalism

questions.q: What false assumption underlies free-market economics, per lesson 1?
a: That people make fully rational financial choices
That governments are always efficient
That wealth is evenly shared
That companies never fail
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the ideology assumes rational decisions, which most of us can't make.

questions.q: What did Merton and Scholes's Nobel-winning work assume?
a: That people always act rationally with money
That markets can never crash
That the state should run companies
That investors need no advice
questions.why: The summary ties their work to the idea of rational financial choice.

questions.q: Why did the Soviet Bloc fail with planning, according to lesson 2?
a: The government had too much authority
It had no plans at all
It trusted private firms too much
It ignored heavy industry
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the problem was too much control; a little guidance can work.

questions.q: What did the South Korean government do in the LG example?
a: Steered it away from textiles toward a better opportunity
Shut the company down
Gave it a monopoly on textiles
Left it entirely alone
questions.why: The summary says the government saw a better opportunity than textiles.

questions.q: What analogy does lesson 3 use for capitalism?
a: A car that needs safety standards
A garden that needs weeding
A ship that needs a captain
A bridge that needs repairs
questions.why: Lesson 3 compares capitalism to a car with seat belts and brakes.
